purpose: Historical argument provenance, not literary keywords. Each passage must be read within its own source and identified reply chain.

av-vi1.question: What counts as a cause of existence, rather than a cause merely of coming-to-be?
av-vi1.immediatePrior: The earlier metaphysical division of being and its concomitants leads to the general division of material, formal, efficient and final causes.
av-vi1.base: The agent as giver of existence is distinguished from a physical principle of motion.
av-vi1.objections: The effect may allegedly cease to need its cause once the cause has produced it, as with a built house.
av-vi1.reply: Only the builder's preparatory activity has ceased; the contingent existent still needs an abiding cause of being for as long as it exists.
av-vi1.continuation: VI.2 answers father/builder/fire counterexamples and distinguishes essential from preparatory causes.
av-vi1.extent: Entire bounded authorial chapter in working English, not fully aligned with the Arabic witness.
av-vi1.missing: Sentence-to-sentence Arabic checking and edition variant collation.

av-vi2.question: Why must an essential cause accompany its effect if builders and parents can disappear?
av-vi2.immediatePrior: VI.1 has established that contingent existence depends on a cause while it exists.
av-vi2.base: An artisan or natural parent is not necessarily the continuing existential cause of the resulting form.
av-vi2.objections: Father-child, builder-house and fire-heat counterexamples; apparent infinite regress of changing conditions.
av-vi2.reply: Preparatory movements and temporal conditions may succeed; essential actual causes accompany their effects. Continuously changing motion avoids the false series of discrete instants.
av-vi2.continuation: VI.3 concerns further causal relations; IX.5 specifies the distinct form-bestowing and material-preparatory levels.
av-vi2.extent: One continuous VI.2 working translation under a single top-level section with several internal subsections.
av-vi2.missing: Collate the Arabic paragraph boundaries and the natural-philosophy arguments on generation.

av-ix5.question: How do sublunary elements obtain differing substantial forms through celestial and separate causes?
av-ix5.immediatePrior: IX.4 develops the order of separate intelligences and celestial causes; VI.2 has distinguished preparatory from abiding efficient causes.
av-ix5.base: Matter receives a determinate readiness through natural/celestial changes and a form from a separate giver.
av-ix5.objections: The theory that elemental differences arise solely from friction, heat, cooling and rarefaction presupposes body without any specific form.
av-ix5.reply: The subject must already be constituted by some form; natural preparation is real but not the whole ontological account.
av-ix5.continuation: IX.6 turns to providence and evil; compare Lāhījī's direct retelling in Gawhar Section V.
av-ix5.extent: Bounded chapter working English; eight Arabic lemmata are anchors rather than a complete aligned original.
av-ix5.sourceVoice: Ibn Sīnā; rival view explicitly reported then criticised
av-ix5.missing: Check full Arabic paragraphs and lexical readings against independent edition.

lah-shaw.part: Shawāriq al-ilhām, vol.I, issues 23 and 24 of the general ontology arguments
lah-shaw.question: Can intrinsically contingent being possess an intrinsic preference or merely extrinsic preponderance that explains actuality short of necessity?
lah-shaw.immediatePrior: The division of necessary, possible and impossible establishes that neither alternative is intrinsically necessary; it does not by itself rule out a weak intrinsic preference.
lah-shaw.base: A contingent effect does not occur unless its existence becomes necessary through its cause.
lah-shaw.objections: Taftāzānī distinguishes several meanings of preference; later objections question whether weak preference is possible and whether an extrinsic cause really necessitates.
lah-shaw.reply: The sufficiency requirement targets preference adequate for occurrence, not every conceivable inclination; the later author's objections and replies must remain attributed.
lah-shaw.continuation: The following lemma concerns antecedent and consequent necessity, which is not translated in this fascicle.
lah-shaw.extent: Two explicitly bounded issues, but the edition prints reported Taftāzānī/Jurjānī/Dawwānī voices rather than independent collations.
lah-shaw.sourceVoice: Lāhījī quoting or paraphrasing Ṭūsī, Taftāzānī, Jurjānī, Dawwānī
lah-shaw.missing: Original editions for every quoted interlocutor and the p.92 problematic negation.

aq-104a.part: Summa theologiae I, quaestio 104, articles 1 and 2
aq-104a.question: Does each creature require conservation by God, and can intermediary creatures conserve?
aq-104a.immediatePrior: Earlier creation theology distinguishes giving esse from imposing a particular new natural form.
aq-104a.base: Every created existent depends continuously on God as primary conserving cause; some effects are also conserved by intermediary causes.
aq-104a.objections: Builder/house counterexample, incorruptible creature, conservation as a new action; then objection that immediate creation entails only immediate conservation.
aq-104a.reply: Conservation is the continuation of the giving of being, not a new movement; created causes may conserve subordinately.
aq-104a.continuation: Articles 3 and 4 distinguish the possibility of annihilation from whether it occurs.
aq-104a.extent: Two complete bounded scholastic articles in English, with source Latin anchors only.
aq-104a.sourceVoice: Aquinas; each article: objections, sed contra, respondeo, replies
aq-104a.missing: Latin variant apparatus; do not assimilate to Avicenna's separate form-bestowing scheme.

aq-104b.part: Summa theologiae I, q.104, articles 3 and 4
aq-104b.question: Can God withhold existence, and does God actually reduce any creature to nothing?
aq-104b.immediatePrior: Articles 1 and 2 establish continuous divine causality and permit subordinated conserving causes.
aq-104b.base: The capacity to withhold existence follows from free divine giving, but Aquinas argues that no creature is in fact annihilated.
aq-104b.objections: Whether free divine agency can cease its sustaining action; whether the finite powers of creatures entail eventual annihilation.
aq-104b.reply: Distinguish a possible act of withdrawal from what God actually does.
aq-104b.continuation: Question 105 treats divine agency in created things.
aq-104b.extent: Two complete scholastic articles in new working English.
aq-104b.missing: Do not treat Aquinas's free will as contained in Avicenna's contingency proof.

lah-eman.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section IV, beginning
lah-eman.locator: Persian pp.290–293 of a chapter continuing to p.297
lah-eman.question: How can the absolutely One produce many beings while remaining simple?
lah-eman.immediatePrior: The preceding demonstrations of causal simplicity and a Necessary Existent.
lah-eman.base: One effect proceeds directly; derivative aspects of the first intellect mediate multiplicity.
lah-eman.objections: Direct plurality would require distinct respects in the absolute One; explanatory intermediaries appear to violate divine causal unity.
lah-eman.reply: Derived respects belong to the first intellect; intermediaries do not independently originate existence.
lah-eman.continuation: The original chapter continues pp.294–297 with revealed language, ten-intellect count, Ṭūsī's reading, and Suhrawardī's fixed-star objection, now restored in a separate continuation record.
lah-eman.extent: ONLY the opening pp.290–293 of an eight-page chapter. Not a complete chapter by itself.
lah-eman.sourceVoice: Lāhījī with a reported philosophers' proof; later attribution to Ṭūsī and Suhrawardī is in continuation
lah-eman.missing: Must be read together with lah-eman-cont pp.294–297.

lah-eman-cont.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section IV, conclusion
lah-eman-cont.locator: Persian pp.294–297, directly accessible page-linked text
lah-eman-cont.question: What supports the identification of the first intellect, how fixed is the ten-intellect count, and what answers Suhrawardī's plurality objection?
lah-eman-cont.immediatePrior: Section IV pp.290–293 proves one immediate emanation and derivative plurality through intelligible respects.
lah-eman-cont.base: The count ten is not proved to be a maximum; multiple effects can follow in the third level through ordered mediating relations.
lah-eman-cont.objections: Reported Suhrawardian complaint that early intellects lack enough respects to account for fixed stars.
lah-eman-cont.reply: Lāhījī introduces twelve third-level possibilities from distinct indirect channels; this undermines the simple objection but is not a physical count.
lah-eman-cont.continuation: Section V immediately tests the causal theory against elemental forms, mixture and Avicenna's hylomorphic refutation of friction-only physics.
lah-eman-cont.extent: Working page-ordered English for the complete omitted four-page continuation.
lah-eman-cont.sourceVoice: Lāhījī, exegetical reports, Rāzī in tafsīr as reported, Ṭūsī gloss as reported, Suhrawardī objection as reported
lah-eman-cont.missing: Independent verification of the Rāzī, Ṭūsī and Suhrawardī original loci; no manuscript collation.

lah-element.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section V
lah-element.locator: Persian pp.298–300, immediately after IV and before VI
lah-element.question: Why do the four elements have different species forms and how do their mixtures prepare composite natural forms?
lah-element.immediatePrior: Section IV argues for multiple effects through a structured order of intellects.
lah-element.base: The view that friction alone produces the elements presupposes a body constituted without any specific form.
lah-element.objections: An unnamed group's friction and cooling hypothesis is reported by Avicenna then rejected by him as retold by Lāhījī.
lah-element.reply: The separate intellect bestows forms in concert with celestial/natural preparations; distinct mixtures prepare matter for further composite species.
lah-element.continuation: Section VI asks why the specific tenth intellect, rather than an earlier or horizontal species-lord, explains the plurality of rational souls and natural forms.
lah-element.extent: Previously omitted complete three-page working contextual English rendering of Section V.
lah-element.sourceVoice: Lāhījī narrates Ibn Sīnā's quotation of an unnamed group, his objection and replacement explanation
lah-element.missing: Independent comparison of the *Shifāʾ* and *Mabdaʾ wa-l-maʿād* source text beyond the existing working IX.5.

lah-active.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section VI
lah-active.question: Which separate principle causes rational souls and natural forms when individuals of one species are numerically many?
lah-active.immediatePrior: Section V has argued that the elements' material dispositions, mixtures and composite forms cannot be explained by friction alone.
lah-active.base: The tenth intellect causes the specific form of rational souls and natural kinds, while their numerical individuation depends on differentiated preparedness of bodies.
lah-active.objections: First Cause alone, first intellect, or celestial bodies cannot explain multiplicity of individuals in one species in the manner assumed.
lah-active.reply: The tenth intellect is positioned at the relevant sublunary level, and different respects and material conditions account for species/individual differences.
lah-active.continuation: Section VII explains why contingent temporal events can arise under an eternal causal order.
lah-active.extent: Entire short Section VI in working English with Persian print source-linked.
lah-active.sourceVoice: Lāhījī; draws on Ibn Sīnā and Illuminationist species-lords as reported
lah-active.missing: Precise medieval source genealogy of the 'lords of species' critique.

lah-temporal.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section VII
lah-temporal.question: How is this event produced at its precise time by an order rooted in eternal causes?
lah-temporal.immediatePrior: Section VI assigns specific forms and souls to the tenth intellect; the present question concerns when the matter becomes prepared.
lah-temporal.base: Distinguish the cause of existence itself from the additional cause that specifies the time of a temporally novel event.
lah-temporal.objections: Why does an event not follow an eternally complete cause at once? Would a regress of new causes be required?
lah-temporal.reply: A continuous motion yields varying dispositions, with proximate preparedness specifying a time and existential effusion following the completed conditions.
lah-temporal.continuation: Section VIII turns to divine willing, intent, satisfaction, and the good resulting from actions.
lah-temporal.extent: Entire short Persian Section VII (pp.304–306) in working English.
lah-temporal.sourceVoice: Lāhījī contrasts philosophers and theologians in the causal-ground question
lah-temporal.missing: Independent verification of quoted general scholastic positions; historical celestial astronomy remains a presupposition.

lah-divine.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section VIII
lah-divine.question: Can the First Cause will the benefit of others without acquiring perfection for himself?
lah-divine.immediatePrior: Section VII established existential and temporal causal dependence; this chapter examines the mode and goal of highest agency.
lah-divine.base: Lāhījī distinguishes a non-acquisitive divine approval or riḍā from a deliberative qaṣd seeking an end for the agent.
lah-divine.objections: How can a perfect agent intend benefit without gaining perfection? Theologians dispute whether purposes in divine acts are valid.
lah-divine.reply: He offers a possible terminological reconciliation with some Muʿtazilī positions, while rejecting blind natural compulsion.
lah-divine.continuation: The next textual division begins after p.309 and has not been included in the present segment.
lah-divine.extent: Entire short Section VIII with explicit voice shifts in working English.
lah-divine.sourceVoice: Lāhījī reports philosophers, Ashʿarī and Muʿtazilī positions with his own proposed reconciliation
lah-divine.missing: Direct independent editions of the theological positions he generalizes.

lah-sarmaya.part: Sarmāya-i īmān, section on contingency, preference, and causal dependence
lah-sarmaya.locator: Persian pp.37–38; argument continues around p.39
lah-sarmaya.question: Why does possible existence need a cause for its continuance?
lah-sarmaya.immediatePrior: Dispute over whether a weaker preference than necessity can explain actual existence.
lah-sarmaya.base: Continuing need derives from intrinsic possibility, not merely temporal origination.
lah-sarmaya.objections: Builder/potter analogy: their effects remain after their actions cease.
lah-sarmaya.reply: Builders effect movements and preparations, not the continuing existence of the composite in the relevant respect.
lah-sarmaya.continuation: The p.39 follow-on needs boundary checking before describing the unit as complete.
lah-sarmaya.extent: Two-page bounded passage; not demonstrated as the full historical chapter.
lah-sarmaya.sourceVoice: Lāhījī in an independent Persian short creed
lah-sarmaya.missing: Collate the full preceding and subsequent textual division of this creed.

taft-mental.question: Must the object of conception have a mode of mental existence, or is an intentional relation enough?
taft-mental.immediatePrior: Proofs appeal to universals, absent objects and affirmative predication.
taft-mental.base: The intelligible content's determination differs from an external instantiation.
taft-mental.objections: Understanding heat would heat the intellect; contemplating the heavens would require enormous space; nonexistents in mind would be external.
taft-mental.reply: Mental representation lacks the physical effects and individuating status of extra-mental heat/heavens.
taft-mental.continuation: Surrounding logical and ontological premises are not fully translated and must be restored from earlier pages.
taft-mental.extent: Selected p.78 introduction, and p.79 objection/reply; no complete full chapter.
taft-mental.missing: Full contiguous context and independent al-Ījī witness.

jurj-mental.part: al-Mawāqif / Sharḥ al-Mawāqif, composite edition vol.VI
jurj-mental.question: If mental form is present, do physical contrary qualities and celestial magnitude inhabit the intellect?
jurj-mental.immediatePrior: Arguments about cognition and mental existence in the matn and sharḥ.
jurj-mental.base: Differentiation between the individual external reality and the known quiddity.
jurj-mental.objections: Knowledge of black/white would instantiate contraries; apprehending a mountain exceeds mind's dimensions.
jurj-mental.reply: The mental form is not the external hāwiyya with physical accidents; the latter is what cannot inhabit the intellect.
jurj-mental.continuation: Anonymous marginal responses need attribution and surrounding text from each gloss.
jurj-mental.extent: Two printed pages in a composite text; not an independently separated edition of each gloss.
jurj-mental.sourceVoice: al-Ījī matn, al-Jurjānī sharḥ, anonymous glosses NOT assigned individually to Siyālkūtī or Ḥalabī
jurj-mental.missing: Visual audit of column/footnote separation and full surrounding commentarial sequence.

taha-jal.question: Does the maker produce a thing simpliciter or produce the relation of a quiddity's existing?
taha-jal.immediatePrior: Technical distinction between simple and compound making in a lexicon.
taha-jal.base: The entry reports conflicting doctrines, quoting Mīr Zāhid's gloss on Sharḥ al-Mawāqif.
taha-jal.objections: Making quiddity itself seems circular; making existence a separate object threatens regress or conceptualism.
taha-jal.reply: Opposed arguments are catalogued; the lexicon is not itself an adjudicated independent Mīr Zāhid edition.
taha-jal.continuation: Original Mīr Zāhid ḥāshiya and the named Sullam glosses require extraction in their own contexts.
taha-jal.extent: Two-page lexical argument entry only; cited earlier voice is mediated.
taha-jal.sourceVoice: Tahānawī is direct; Mīr Zāhid nested quotation/report, not independently collated
taha-jal.missing: Direct Mīr Zāhid witness and its matn and scholastic reply.

astar-choice.part: al-Barāhīn al-qāṭiʿa, vol.II, discussion of divine power and causal modality
astar-choice.question: Can the full cause necessitate the act without abolishing genuine divine power or choice?
astar-choice.immediatePrior: Definition of divine power as ability to act and refrain under relevant considerations.
astar-choice.base: An effect is possible in itself, necessary given a completed cause, impossible when required causes are absent.
astar-choice.objections: Qūshjī's reported answer faces al-Khafrī's objection: if divine will is identical with essence, how can it be otherwise? A Khwānsārī point probes the temporal object.
astar-choice.reply: The later author explores newly arising will or a distinct temporal object; quoted voices cannot be treated as verified originals.
astar-choice.continuation: Check subsequent and preceding pages of the printed author; separately collate Qūshjī/Khafrī/Jamāl Khwānsārī.
astar-choice.extent: Argument reported in a later author; independent editions of cited historical interlocutors missing.
astar-choice.sourceVoice: Astarābādī direct; Ṭūsī, Ḥillī, Qūshjī, Khafrī, Āqā Jamāl Khwānsārī mediated
astar-choice.missing: Full source genealogy and page/folio collation of each named speaker.

nara-actual.part: al-Lamaʿāt al-ʿarshiyya, separate arguments about existence and quiddity
nara-actual.question: If existence is primary, how can quiddity be distinguished without reifying two external entities?
nara-actual.immediatePrior: Existence/quiddity predication and the question whether existence attaches to a prior thing.
nara-actual.base: Particular existence is primary in actuality; quiddity is abstracted from determinate limiting aspects.
nara-actual.objections: If existence precedes quiddity, predicate precedes subject; if subsequent, regress; if separate, no unity.
nara-actual.reply: The attribution is intellectual; external actual individuality is not two self-standing objects.
nara-actual.continuation: The omitted pp.73–81 must not be silently bridged as one continuous proof.
nara-actual.extent: Two disconnected source excerpts, **not** a contiguous argument, with different contexts.
nara-actual.missing: Acquire and translate pp.73–81 to identify the intervening arguments and transitions.

nara-second.part: Sharḥ Ilāhiyyāt al-Shifāʾ, commentary on metaphysics' subject and attributes
nara-second.locator: Vol.I pp.106–107, plus separate note p.110
nara-second.question: How are general attributes of being distinguished from logical second intentions?
nara-second.immediatePrior: Avicennian account of the subject of metaphysics and shared principles of sciences.
nara-second.base: Being-as-being's concomitants can be distinguished from properties predicated of intelligibles qua intelligible.
nara-second.objections: The proposed criterion risks reducing real attributes to mere classifications.
nara-second.reply: Attributes of second intentions presuppose an intelligible subject; metaphysics has broader subject matter.
nara-second.continuation: p.110 is a separate textual-critical report of a negation, not continuous part of p.106–107.
nara-second.extent: Bounded pp.106–107 with noncontiguous p.110 textual note.
nara-second.sourceVoice: Narāqī with reported opponent and reported copy variants
nara-second.missing: Separate the source's original Avicennian lemma and its commentary in a double-column witness.

khay-fire.part: al-Hadiyya al-saʿīdiyya, reported arguments from original printed pp.92–94
khay-fire.locator: Cairo 1904, quoted in secondary modern history 2023 pp.202–203
khay-fire.question: Does hidden imported fire explain heat, or do local transformations suffice?
khay-fire.immediatePrior: Debate with a latent-fire hypothesis in nineteenth-century natural philosophy.
khay-fire.base: Arguments from friction, sealed vessels, pressure and ice challenge occult influx accounts of thermal change.
khay-fire.objections: Claim that incoming subtle fire is required for change.
khay-fire.reply: Cited experiments and cases support transformation in the medium; modern physical truth is not settled.
khay-fire.continuation: The original 1904 print and wider motion/time/atoms chapters remain uncollated.
khay-fire.extent: Modern quotation with historical page attribution, not direct 1904 text.
khay-fire.sourceVoice: Khayrābādī as represented by a modern writer, not an independently read original
khay-fire.missing: Original 1904 Arabic source, full chapter, and distinguishing Faḍl-i Ḥaqq from other Khayrābādīs.

lah-making.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Sections I–II
lah-making.question: What is meant by ijād, takwīn, ibdāʿ and jaʿl, and does the maker directly produce quiddity, existence or the attribution of one to the other?
lah-making.immediatePrior: Book II of Gawhar examines the Necessary Existent and divine attributes; Book III opens the theory of divine action and production.
lah-making.base: Lāhījī reports divergent use of creation terms, then favors simple making of actual quiddity understood as something externally issued by its cause rather than making a separately real general concept of existence.
lah-making.objections: An existence-first thesis may merely rename the issued actuality; an attribution-first thesis threatens self-explanatory relata or indefinite regress. A fourth version, making a thing be its own essence, is rejected.
lah-making.reply: The meaning of existence is abstracted from the quiddity's actuality; production of the actual thing already explains why it exists. Avicenna's apricot formulation is quoted and interpreted by Lāhījī, NOT an independently collated Avicennian original.
lah-making.continuation: Section III pp.283–289 asks how the effect relates to the First, including a report and critique of accounts of waḥdat al-wujūd.
lah-making.extent: Connected five-page working English across two distinct full historical sections, with source page links and voice tags. No complete Persian manuscript collation.
lah-making.sourceVoice: Lāhījī himself, with philosophers/theologians compared and a reported Avicenna–Bahmanyār exchange
lah-making.missing: Independent Avicennian apricot source and cross-edition Persian collations; compare precise Lāhījī Shawāriq question instead of assuming textual identity.

lah-unity.part: Gawhar-i murād, Article II, Book III, Section III
lah-unity.question: In what sense does an effect proceed from its cause, and can divine unity of existence be understood without making all created individuals numerically identical?
lah-unity.immediatePrior: Sections I–II established what is produced and distinguished the conceptual predicate 'exists' from an additional made entity.
lah-unity.base: A report of the Sufis describes ta-jallī and unity; Lāhījī distinguishes experiential claims, conceptual reconstructions, the Necessary as self-subsistent ground and contingent realities as derivative.
lah-unity.objections: An analogy with an indeterminate natural universal would require the Necessary Reality to receive finite determinations to exist; Lāhījī objects that necessary existence is precisely not dependent on such determinations.
lah-unity.reply: Multiple created realities receive their existence through relation to one unconditioned reality; the text resists simply identifying that ground with each finite individual. A further speculative collective-unity analogy is attributed to unnamed authorities and not simply endorsed.
lah-unity.continuation: Section IV pp.290–297 moves to the Rule of the One, separate intellects and Suhrawardī's fixed-star objection.
lah-unity.extent: Full seven-page bounded historical section in continuous page order as working English. Reports and commentary distinguished; not an independently collated Persian archetype.
lah-unity.sourceVoice: Lāhījī reports Sufi doctrine and philosophical reconstructions, objects to one analogy, gives a differentiated account and cites unnamed eminent writers
lah-unity.missing: Textual/terminological comparison with Ṣadrā's independent Asfār discussions; direct verification of cited Sufi/Akbarian passages.

nara-presence.part: Jāmiʿ al-afkār wa-nāqid al-anẓār, vol. II, divine knowledge, first inquiry, third way, first preliminary
nara-presence.locator: Arabic edited print pp.25–27. The preliminary and third proof continue after p.27.
nara-presence.question: How can the subject apprehend itself and its bodily faculties without an added representative image?
nara-presence.immediatePrior: The preceding distinction between acquired conceptual knowledge and the object existing outside the mind; prior senses and abstraction argument.
nara-presence.base: The intellectual subject's awareness of itself is grounded in immediate presence, not an added universal representation.
nara-presence.objections: Faculty differences might be due only to varying impairments; perhaps a stronger imaginative or estimative power eventually apprehends universals.
nara-presence.reply: Narāqī answers the faculty objection conditionally, distinguishes immaterial intellection, then uses uniquely indexical self-knowledge, a regress of representing images, pain and bodily-faculty awareness to motivate presential cognition.
nara-presence.continuation: The awareness of particular images and faculties continues on the next page; a second preliminary through Bahmanyār and the conclusion of divine knowledge follow much later.
nara-presence.extent: Three consecutive checked printed pages with selected original anchors and argument-level translations; no full third proof or line-aligned Arabic.
nara-presence.sourceVoice: Narāqī is the direct author; the 'if it is said' opponents are anonymous as reported by him.
nara-presence.missing: Printed pp.28 onward; Bahmanyār source in al-Taḥṣīl; independently source direct Ṣadrian presential knowledge passages and later Qajar replies.

sabz-motion.part: Sharḥ al-Manẓūma / Ghurar al-farāʾid, natural philosophy, section/ghurar no.111
sabz-motion.locator: Modern annotated printed vol. IV pp.301–302 and 305; pp.303–304 were not independently accessed.
sabz-motion.question: How can substantial motion have a persistent subject if the natural substance itself flows?
sabz-motion.immediatePrior: Earlier ghurar on body, matter, form, and which categories admit movement, especially no.110 immediately preceding.
sabz-motion.base: The substantial nature's real existence is a flowing actuality and need not have a separate stationary substantial subject.
sabz-motion.objections: Avicenna's Physics II.3 argues either an underlying species remains (then only an accident changes) or it does not (then every intermediate stage is a new substance).
sabz-motion.reply: The later passage reframes the subject as the intrinsically flowing existence itself; the further subject-in-matter qualification invokes continuous individual determinations, but the modern annotator's notes cannot be conflated with Sabzavārī.
sabz-motion.continuation: Following ghurar no.112 addresses numerical/specific unity of motion; missing pp.303–304 of no.111 remain uncollated.
sabz-motion.extent: Connected beginning pp.301–302 and separate p.305 only; printed witness has Sabzavārī and Hasan Ḥasanzāda Āmulī interleaved.
sabz-motion.sourceVoice: Sabzavārī's introductory verse certain; printed exposition may include later Hasan Ḥasanzāda Āmulī remarks marked (ح.ح); Avicenna is quoted within the printed source.
sabz-motion.missing: Directly inspect pp.303–304, mark exact verse/commentator/gloss divisions and compare a pre-Ḥasanzāda print plus original Physics II.3.

works: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī — Ḥall mushkilāt al-Ishārāt
families.task: Translate the common Avicennian lemma plus Rāzī's objection, Ṭūsī's answer and Quṭb's adjudication as one documented debate.

families.title: The Tajrīd, Kashf and Sharḥ commentary trees
works: Dawwānī, Dashtakī, al-Khafrī, Lāhījī and later superglosses
families.task: Always anchor each commentary to the identical matn sentence and distinguish opposite disputants and reported testimony.

families.title: Post-Rāzian philosophical kalām
works: Siyālkūtī, Ḥasan Çelebi, Ḥalabī and other gloss layers
families.task: Separate matn, sharḥ, gloss and cited objection; identify the epistemic thesis actually being disputed.

families.title: Shamsiyya, second intentions and disputation
works: Shams al-Dīn al-Samarqandī — works on logic and ādāb al-baḥth
Indian, Ottoman and North African supercommentaries
families.task: Treat logical arguments and philosophy of language as primary parts of late Avicennism, not metaphysical appendices.

families.title: Illuminationist revisions and responses
works: Ibn Kammūna — commentaries and al-Jadīd fī l-ḥikma
Quṭb al-Dīn al-Shīrāzī — Sharḥ Ḥikmat al-ishrāq
families.task: Compare logical, ontological and epistemic revisions with their precise Avicennian target.

families.title: Akbarian philosophical and theological encounters
works: Jāmī and later Akbarian interpretive works
families.task: Trace explicit borrowings and disagreements on wujūd, causality and divine knowledge; do not equate every use of tajallī with numerical monism.

families.title: Late Timurid and Shiraz disputations
works: Ghiyāth al-Dīn Manṣūr al-Dashtakī — philosophical works
families.task: Separate the Dawwānī–Dashtakī exchange from al-Sayyid al-Sanad (generally Jurjānī).

families.title: Safavid Isfahan and competing Avicennisms
works: Mullā Ṣadrā — al-Asfār and Shifāʾ glosses
Mullā Muḥsin Fayḍ and Rajab ʿAlī Tabrīzī
Lāhījī, Khwānsārī and Sabzawārī correspondence and glosses
families.task: Distinguish Ṣadrian new metaphysics from the independent Peripatetic and kalām responses of his contemporaries. The later Narāqī/Sabzavārī reception of Ṣadrian issues is crosslinked separately from this Safavid stream, not reclassified as Safavid contemporaries.

families.title: Late Persian, Qajar and Tehran school
works: Muḥammad Mahdī al-Narāqī — Jāmiʿ al-afkār, Lamaʿāt
Mullā ʿAlī Nūrī and Mullā Hādī Sabzawārī
families.task: Recover direct texts on substantial motion, particular existence, soul and physics, instead of assigning group-level doctrines. Direct Narāqī *Jāmiʿ al-afkār* II:25–27 and Sabzavārī *Sharḥ al-Manẓūma* IV:301–302, 305 are now bounded working dossiers, NOT complete surrounding proofs.

families.title: Ottoman and Kurdish-province Hidāya chain
families.task: Work through one full Hidāya lemma, Maybudī's commentary, Lārī's gloss, later reply and Turkish translation before claiming the doctrine settled.

families.title: South Asian Shifāʾ, Mawāqif and Dars-e-Niẓāmī
works: Qāḍī Mubārak Shāh and further ḥawāshī
Safavid Shifāʾ commentary manuscripts preserved in India
families.task: Differentiate historical authors and manuscript copy/transmission from original composition; do not confuse Faḍl-i Ḥaqq and Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq.

families.title: Western Islamic logic and Khūnajī's Jumal
works: Ibn Wāṣil / Urmawī lines received westward
families.task: The western logic tradition was broadly post-Avicennian but not a mere copy of eastern al-Shamsiyya teaching.

families.title: Modern editorial and teaching continuations
works: Persian explanatory commentary on the Ishārāt
Critical editions of medieval and early modern scholastic works
Modern philosophical reconstruction and reception studies
families.task: Place contemporary scholarship apart from historical authorial witnesses; distinguish modern pedagogy from new primary doctrinal positions.

requirements: Historical family -> base work -> work division -> chapter/masʾala -> identical lemma -> objections/replies
Direct witness or later author's report labelled without substitution
Original-language translation from enough consecutive context, not keyword snippets
Variant collation and edition page/folio independently checked
Reader comparison justified explicitly, with connection and difference
Unsupported families displayed as unedited, not absent from history

statusLegend.partial-primary: Bounded material present but no complete family corpus
statusLegend.no-primary-unit: No directly translated primary unit in current corpus
statusLegend.untranslated-original: Named original texts not independently translated
statusLegend.topic-only: Some related concepts present but not adequate primary coverage

minimumCompleteArgument: base author's exact question and heading

statusCodes.contextual-rendering-checked-pages: Direct page sequence inspected; working contextual English, not line-by-line source collation
statusCodes.working-translation-unverified: Described as a full working unit, but no sentence-level verification completed
statusCodes.selective-excerpt: Only a subsection or objection/reply translated
statusCodes.noncontiguous-selective: Separate passages with missing intervening pages
statusCodes.nested-report: Original historical author only represented through a later writer
statusCodes.layered-attribution-uncertain: Mixed matn, sharḥ and anonymous glosses
statusCodes.mediated-quotation: Historical excerpt quoted in a modern source, original not read

notes: Gawhar II.III Sections I-VIII pp278–309 now have connected working English treatments in eight linked source files. Their historical printed sections remain separate; do not conflate this with all of the 758-page book or a manuscript-critical edition.
